legend: Jenga is a game played by two or more players. They start with a tower of n$$$n$$$ rows, each row consists of 3$$$3$$$ rectangular blocks. Then they remove blocks one by one until the tower falls. The player which breaks the tower loses. Removed blocks are usually placed on top of the tower forming the new row; however, in this problem, we'll consider a modified version of the game: removed blocks are put aside and are never returned to the tower.

Monocarp and Polycarp play Jenga a lot. They noticed that a tower row remains stable if it contains either the two side blocks, or the central block. Of course, if there are any additional blocks in the row, it is also stable. Thus, rows xxx, x.x, xx., .xx, .x. are stable, while rows x.., ..x and ... are unstable. Here and further on, the character 'x' depicts a block which is not removed yet, and '.' represents an empty space after removing a block. If at least one row (even the topmost one) in the tower becomes unstable, the tower immediately falls.

Currently, Monocarp and Polycarp have a tower of n$$$n$$$ rows, where some blocks may already be removed (but each row is stable). It is Monocarp's turn now. Given the state of the tower (which blocks are removed and which are still present), you have to determine who wins, assuming both players play optimally.
input: The first line contains one integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤5⋅104$$$1 \le t \le 5 \cdot 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains one integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤5⋅104$$$1 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^4$$$) — the number of rows in the tower.

Then, n$$$n$$$ lines follow, the i$$$i$$$-th of them contains 6$$$6$$$ characters in the format ***=== or ===***, where each '*' is either 'x' or '.' — the state of the i$$$i$$$-th row from the top. Rows ***=== and ===*** alternate, describing the Jenga tower.
Additional constraints on the input: the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 5⋅104$$$5 \cdot 10^4$$$, and each row of the tower is stable.
output: For each test case, print Monocarp if Monocarp wins; otherwise, print Polycarp.
note: In the first test case, Monocarp should remove the central block from the bottom row. After this, it is possible to remove only two blocks from the Jenga tower: the first block from the first row and the third block from the third row. If any other block is removed, the tower falls. Whatever block Polycarp removes, Monocarp takes the other one, leaving Polycarp with no choice.
In the second test case, no blocks can be removed without breaking Jenga. So, Polycarp wins.
In the third test case, Monocarp has a winning strategy.
The fourth test case represents the configuration shown in the picture.

legend.ai: 叠叠乐是一种由两名或更多玩家参与的游戏。游戏开始时，他们面前有一座由 n$$$n$$$ 层组成的塔，每层由 3$$$3$$$ 块长方体积木组成。随后，他们逐块移除积木，直到塔倒塌。导致塔倒塌的玩家输掉游戏。通常，被移除的积木会放在塔顶，组成新的一层；不过在本题中，我们考虑该游戏的一个变体：被移除的积木会被放在一旁，永远不会重新放回塔中。

Monocarp 和 Polycarp 经常玩叠叠乐。他们注意到，如果某一层中包含两块侧边积木，或者包含中间的积木，那么这一层就能保持稳定。当然，如果这一层中还有其他积木，它也能保持稳定。因此，xxx、x.x、xx.、.xx、.x. 这些层是稳定的，而 x..、..x 和 ... 这些层不稳定。下文中，字符 'x' 表示尚未被移除的积木，'.' 表示移除积木后留下的空位。如果塔中至少有一层（即使是最顶层）变得不稳定，塔就会立即倒塌。
现在，Monocarp 和 Polycarp 有一座由 n$$$n$$$ 层组成的塔，其中一些积木可能已经被移除(但每一层都保持稳定)。现在轮到 Monocarp 行动。给定塔的状态(哪些积木已被移除，哪些仍然存在)，假设两位玩家都采取最优策略，你需要判断谁会获胜。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤5⋅104$$$1 \le t \le 5 \cdot 10^4$$$)——测试用例的数量。
每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤5⋅104$$$1 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^4$$$)——塔中的行数。
接下来是 n$$$n$$$ 行，其中第 i$$$i$$$ 行包含 6$$$6$$$ 个字符，格式为 ***=== 或 ===***，其中每个 '*' 要么是 'x'，要么是 '.' ——从顶部开始第 i$$$i$$$ 行的状态。***=== 和 ===*** 两种行交替出现，描述了这座叠叠乐塔。
输入的额外约束：所有测试用例中 n$$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 5⋅104$$$5 \cdot 10^4$$$，且塔的每一行都处于稳定状态。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，如果 Monocarp 获胜，则输出 Monocarp；否则输出 Polycarp。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，Monocarp 应移除最底行中央的方块。此后，叠叠乐塔中只有两个方块可以被移除：第一行的第一个方块和第三行的第三个方块。如果移除任何其他方块，塔就会倒塌。无论 Polycarp 移除哪个方块，Monocarp 都会拿走另一个，从而让 Polycarp 毫无选择。
在第二个测试用例中，不破坏叠叠乐的情况下无法移除任何方块。因此，Polycarp 获胜。
在第三个测试用例中，Monocarp 有必胜策略。
第四个测试用例表示图片中所示的配置。
